about: CHAIN saga_northumbria_irish_sea: THE SAINT ON THE ROAD (Design/content/CHAINS.md; page Design/content/chains/saga_northumbria_irish_sea.md; words Data/writing/chain_saga_northumbria_irish_sea.json). The saga of Northumbria and the Irish Sea, 875 to 883: Bishop Eardulf and Abbot Eadred leave Lindisfarne with Saint Cuthbert's body before Halfdan's army, wander seven years with seven bearers and a cart, try to sail for Ireland from the Derwent's mouth and are turned back by a storm that takes the gospel book, find the book on the sands at Whithorn, and end by having the army buy a slave boy, Guthred son of Harthacnut, from a widow and make him king (Historia de Sancto Cuthberto 12-13, 20; Symeon, Libellus ii.6, ii.10-13; Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 875, 876; Annals of Ulster 877, 878). Fourteen cards: eleven steps (s01 to s11: nine harbour, one sea, one crew) and three endings. Step flags ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_1 .. _11 and ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_on (the chain is begun: set by step 1 or step 2). What the player did: _ferried, _bought, _alms, _reeves_eyes, _saints_eyes, _plate, _boy_aboard, _fed_army, _counted, _ketil_friend, _pilot, _iona_letter, _shrine_carried, _hull_promised, _warned, _turned_back, _book_lost, _book_saved, _found_book, _saint_in_ireland, _boy_free, _boy_baptised, _boy_sold, _lent, _spoke, _boy_given, _boy_sold_dear, _boy_kept. Endings: ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_end_oswigesdune (what happened), ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_end_ireland (history changed: changed_cuthbert_in_ireland), ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_end_ships_boy (history changed: changed_guthred_never_king); ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_done closes the chain. Lasting costs: ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_sold_a_king, ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_blamed_in_northumbria, ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_saint_denied. Each option's note names its outcome text. Written 6 Oct 2026; a draft for the user to overwrite. (?) marks what could not be checked.

cards.note: Step 1, the start (drawn at Lindisfarena, 875 to 876). Bishop Eardulf (bishop 854 to 899) and Eadred, abbot of Carlisle, take up Saint Cuthbert's body with Oswald's head, some of Aidan's bones and the bones of three bishops, 241 years after the founding, because Halfdan lies on the Tyne (Symeon, Libellus de exordio ii.6; Historia de Sancto Cuthberto 20; dossiers/lindisfarena.md section 5). Seven bearers, four of them named: Hunred, Stitheard, Edmund, Franco (Libellus ii.12, by the dossier's count xxvii). That a merchant's boat took the coffin over the water is invented; the tide road to the island is real. Cast: Eardulf, Eadred, Hunred (all real). Sets ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_1 and ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_on; _ferried, _bought or _alms.

cards.note: Step 2 (scheduled twenty days after step 1; also drawn at Bebbanburg 875 to 877, where it can begin the chain for a player who missed the island). The lord of the rock will not take the saint in. Sources: kings 'beyond the Tyne' under the army, Ricsige to 876 and Ecgberht II after (Historia regum 873, 876; realms/northumbria_york.json rulers); Halfdan 'fixed his winter-quarters by the river Tine' (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 875, Ingram 1823, by way of dossiers/gyrwe.md). That Bamburgh refused the body is invented (?): the sources say only that the bearers went from place to place and found no rest. The reeve is invented, unnamed; Stitheard is one of the four named bearers (real name). Sets ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_2 and ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_on; _reeves_eyes or _saints_eyes.

cards.note: Step 3, a turn (scheduled by step 2; drawn at Gyrwe 875 to 876). Halfdan's part of the great army lies on the Tyne, sells what it has taken, and sells a boy. Sources: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 875 ('fixed his winter-quarters by the river Tine', Ingram 1823) and 876; Symeon, Libellus ii.6 (Halfdan entering the Tyne with a fleet); Historia de Sancto Cuthberto 13: Guthred son of Harthacnut, a boy whom the Danes had sold as a slave to a widow at Whittingham. When and where he was sold is not recorded: the game puts the sale in the Tyne camp in these years (?). That Jarrow's church was burned in 875 is tradition, not Symeon's word (dossiers/gyrwe.md) (?): the card says only a church without a roof. Cast: Guthred (real); Ketil, a shipman of Halfdan's (invented; Ketill is a common Norse name); the widow's man (invented, unnamed). Sets ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_3; _plate, _boy_aboard, _fed_army or _counted. Buying the boy is the seed of both changed endings.

cards.note: Step 5, a turn, optional (drawn at Hi 878 to 879). In 878 the shrine of Columba and his other relics came to Ireland in flight from the foreigners (Annals of Ulster 878, paraphrased; dossiers/hi.md section 5). Feradach was abbot of Hi, died 880 (dossiers/hi.md). Lindisfarne was founded from this island by Aidan in 635, and some of Aidan's bones were in Cuthbert's coffin (Bede, Historia ecclesiastica III.3, III.26; Symeon ii.6). That Hi wrote to Cuthbert's people offering house room in Ireland is invented, to give the real attempt on Ireland a cause (?). The text given is the Irish quatrain on the rough wind (texts_793.json irish_viking_terror). Cast: Feradach (real); a brother (invented, unnamed). Sets ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_5; _iona_letter, _shrine_carried.

cards.note: Step 6 (drawn at Legacaestir 878 to 881). The bishop and the abbot mean to take the body to Ireland from the mouth of the Derwent, and have told only the oldest and wisest (Symeon, Libellus ii.11; dossiers/lindisfarena.md: 'A ship for Ireland is driven back to the Derwent's mouth'). The year of the attempt is not recorded: the game allows 878 to 881 (?). There is no port for the Derwent on the chart, so the bearers' man looks for a hull at the nearest landing on that sea: Legacaestir, which the Chronicle still calls a waste city in 893 (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 894 for 893; dossiers/legacaestir.md). Hunger on the road, a salted horse's head and one cheese: a story in the Durham tradition (?). Cast: Franco, one of the four named bearers (real name; what he was like is invented). Sets ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_6; _hull_promised or _warned.

cards.note: Step 7 (a sea card, drawn under way once the hull is promised). The crossing. Symeon, Libellus ii.11: the bishop, the abbot and a few went aboard at the Derwent's mouth while the people, who had not been told, wept on the shore; a storm rose, three great waves fell on the ship and the water that came aboard turned to blood; the ship heeled and the gospel book, bound in gold and gems, went into the sea; they put back. The danger warns first: the wind backs before the seas come. The red water is told as the men saw it. History is the first option. Holding on and reaching Ireland is history changed (flag ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_saint_in_ireland; the ending sets changed_cuthbert_in_ireland). Cast: Eardulf, Eadred (real); the player's steersman. Sets ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_7; _turned_back with _book_lost or _book_saved, or _saint_in_ireland.

cards.note: Step 8 (scheduled forty to sixty days after the storm; drawn at Legacaestir while the book is lost, to 883). Hunred's dream. Symeon, Libellus ii.12: Saint Cuthbert appeared to Hunred and told him to look for the book on the shore at the lowest ebb, and to take a bridle he would find hanging on a tree and show it to a horse, which would come and draw the cart; the sea had gone back three miles and the book lay on the sand at Whithorn (Candida Casa) unharmed. The gospel book is by Durham tradition the Lindisfarne Gospels, with staining said to be from sea water (?). The thief of the cheese turned into a fox is a later Durham story (?). There is no port for Whithorn: the card is at the landing where the bearers know the player, and going with Hunred is told in the outcome. The book is found whatever is chosen, as it was. The riddle is Exeter 26, the book (riddles_793.json). Cast: Hunred (real). Sets ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_8; _found_book.

cards.note: Step 10 (drawn at Eoforwic 882 to 883). York has had no king since Halfdan was driven out (realms/northumbria_york.json rulers 877-883); the saint's people have been four months at Crayke, guests of Abbot Geve (Symeon, Libellus ii.13). Abbot Eadred's dream: Saint Cuthbert tells him to go over the Tyne to the army of the Danes, and say that they must find the boy Guthred son of Harthacnut, whom they sold to a widow at Whittingham, pay her the price, and make him king on the hill called Oswigesdune with a gold ring on his right arm (Historia de Sancto Cuthberto 13; our rendering, no words quoted). The 'holds' of the army are the Chronicle's word for its great men (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 905, 910). Cast: Eadred (real); a hold of the army (invented, unnamed); Ketil (invented). Sets ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_10; _lent or _spoke. A player with the boy aboard is sent to step 11.

cards.note: Step 11, only for a player who has the boy aboard (scheduled three days after step 10; also drawn at any of the four Northumbrian ports, 883 to 890, so that he is found). The abbot has come for the boy the saint named, and the boy is yours. Source: Historia de Sancto Cuthberto 13 (the price was to be paid to the widow: here the player stands where she stood). A slave's price of about a pound is the common English figure of the laws (?); 480 pennies, two pounds, is the game's 'king's price' and the house's first debt. Giving him is the honest road and leads to the richest form of the true ending. Keeping him, if he is a free man who can refuse, is history changed: no King Guthred (ending end_ships_boy). Cast: Eadred, Guthred (real). Sets ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_11; _boy_given, _boy_sold_dear with _sold_a_king, or _boy_kept; clears _boy_aboard unless he is kept.

cards.note: ENDING: what happened (scheduled by steps 10 and 11; also drawn at Gyrwe, Eoforwic, Lindisfarena or Bebbanburg, 883 to 890, for anyone who began the chain and did not change it, so no road ends with nothing). Historia de Sancto Cuthberto 13 and Symeon ii.13: the army and the English made Guthred king on Oswigesdune with a gold ring on his right arm and swore peace over the saint's body; the bishop brought the body to Cunecacestre (Chester-le-Street); the king gave the saint all the land between Tyne and Wear and the right that whoever fled to the body should have peace thirty-seven days and nights. Where Oswigesdune was is not known (?): the card lies on the Tyne, in the land that was given. Rewards: unlock_charter_gyrwe (the saint's land is the bishop's to free of toll: he is lord between Tyne and Wear from 883); for those who gave, lent or spoke, unlock_title_st_cuthberts_man as well (a named man of the saint's peace); for the one who gave the boy freely, the king's own gifts: unlock_plot_eoforwic and unlock_title_kings_guest; for returned altar silver, unlock_relic_cuthbert_cloth. Sets ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_end_oswigesdune and ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_done.

king.note: Guthred son of Harthacnut, king 883 to 895; real

cards.title: The gold ring
cards.intention: This year the army and the English together took a king: a young Dane bought out of a widow's yard, with a gold ring on his right arm and the saint's coffin beside him on the hill.

options.label: Take what the king offers the man who gave him up for nothing
options.note: outcome: chain_saga_northumbria_irish_sea.end_oswigesdune.out_kings_friend (the hard road: 1,500 d in arm-rings, the saint's charter on the Tyne, a plot at York, the king's guest)

options.label: Stand among the witnesses as one who lent or spoke, and take the saint's hand for it
options.note: outcome: chain_saga_northumbria_irish_sea.end_oswigesdune.out_witness (900 d, the charter and a name in the saint's peace)

options.label: Lay the altar silver from the Tyne on the new altar
options.note: outcome: chain_saga_northumbria_irish_sea.end_oswigesdune.out_altar (700 d from the king's gift to the church, the charter, and a strip of the cloth that lay on the coffin)

options.label: Ask only the saint's peace for your hull between Tyne and Wear, and the carrying of his first rents
options.note: outcome: chain_saga_northumbria_irish_sea.end_oswigesdune.out_peace (600 d paid forward for carrying the saint's wool, and the charter: every road has this)

memory.kings_friend: gave the king up for nothing
memory.altar: laid the altar silver on the altar

cards.note: ENDING: history changed (scheduled 200 days after a crossing that reached Ireland; also drawn at Hi or Duiblinn from 879). In truth the ship was driven back (Symeon ii.11) and the saint never left Britain. Here he lies in Ireland among Columba's family, whose shrine went over in 878 (Annals of Ulster 878). What follows in later years: no dream at Crayke, so no King Guthred and no peace of 883 (the army takes a king of its own kind); no land between Tyne and Wear for the saint, no thirty-seven days' sanctuary, no Chester-le-Street in 883 and no Durham in 995; the English of the north lose the one lord the Danes feared; the Irish church gains a second great shrine and the pilgrims who follow it. Flann son of Mael Duin was abbot of Hi 880 to 891 (dossiers/hi.md); in 879 the card is too early for him by a year (?). A stranger has no honour-price in Irish law until a king or abbot names him his guest (realms/irish_sea.md, 'Who protects'). Rewards: unlock_title_abbots_guest; with the letter of step 5, unlock_relic_cuthbert_cloth as well (hard road); or unlock_factor_hi; or, with a freed Guthred aboard, unlock_partner_guthred (and changed_guthred_never_king). Lasting cost: ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_blamed_in_northumbria. Sets ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_end_ireland, changed_cuthbert_in_ireland, ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_done.

abbot.note: Flann son of Mael Duin, abbot of Hi 880 to 891; real

cards.title: Two saints in one house
cards.intention: Cuthbert of the English lies in Ireland now, a day's walk from Columba's shrine, and the bearer who carried him seven years has learned to ask for bread in Irish.

options.label: Take the abbot's protection: his guest on every shore where Columba's word runs
options.note: outcome: chain_saga_northumbria_irish_sea.end_ireland.out_guest (800 d in arm-rings from a king of Mide, and an honour-price in Ireland)

options.label: You carried the letter that called them: ask for the abbot's protection, and a strip of the saint's cloth for your house
options.note: outcome: chain_saga_northumbria_irish_sea.end_ireland.out_cloth (the hard road: 1,000 d, the protection and a relic the house keeps)

options.label: Ask for no honour: only to be the man who brings the wine for Columba's houses
options.note: outcome: chain_saga_northumbria_irish_sea.end_ireland.out_cellar (600 d, a wine commission at a high premium, and the cellarer of Hi as your factor)

options.label: Take the protection, and swear fellowship here with Harthacnut's son, whom nobody now will come to buy
options.note: outcome: chain_saga_northumbria_irish_sea.end_ireland.out_fellow (800 d, the protection, and a sworn partner who would have been a king)

cards.note: ENDING: history changed (scheduled sixty days after step 11's refusal; drawn at any port after it). In truth the army paid the widow and made Guthred king in 883 (Historia de Sancto Cuthberto 13); he ruled twelve years, gave the saint the land between Tyne and Wear, and was buried in York minster on 24 August 895 (Aethelweard iv.3). Here he has refused, as a free man, to be bought a second time. What follows in later years: the army at York takes a heathen king of its own choosing; there is no sworn peace between Dane and English in 883 and no grant to the saint; the saint's people stay at Crayke on an abbot's charity and Chester-le-Street is not founded; the first Christian king of the Danes of York comes a generation late or not at all. His kin at York are the game's invention: the History names his father and nothing more (?). The felag, a sworn fellowship of shared goods, is the Norse merchants' own form (CHAINS.md unlock_partner). Rewards: unlock_partner_guthred, or unlock_kin_guthred_foster, or unlock_plot_eoforwic. Lasting cost: ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_saint_denied. Sets ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_end_ships_boy, changed_guthred_never_king, ch_saga_northumbria_irish_sea_done.

kinsman.note: a man of his father's kin from York; invented, unnamed

cards.title: Not bought twice
cards.intention: The army at York has shouted for another king, and the saint is still a guest at Crayke. A grey Dane has come down to your hull with a bag of arm-rings for the son of a friend he thought was dead.

options.label: Swear fellowship: his kin's silver buys a second hull, and he sails it
options.note: outcome: chain_saga_northumbria_irish_sea.end_ships_boy.out_felag (700 d as your half of the common purse, and a sworn partner with a second boat)

options.label: Take him into the house as a foster-son, with his kin's gift for his keeping
options.note: outcome: chain_saga_northumbria_irish_sea.end_ships_boy.out_foster (900 d, and kin among the Danes of York)

options.label: Send him to York with his rings and your good word, and ask a plot on the river from his kin
options.note: outcome: chain_saga_northumbria_irish_sea.end_ships_boy.out_york (600 d and a plot at York; he is a great man's son again, and still not a king)
